items.teaser: Russian forces attacked Zaporizhzhia with guided aerial bombs, striking a five-story residential building. At least two people were killed, others were injured, and an unknown number of people may be trapped beneath the rubble.

items.title: France condemns strikes on Pryluky and Kramatorsk: Russian crimes cannot go unpunished
items.teaser: France has condemned Russian strikes on a residential building in Pryluky and two buses in Kramatorsk that reportedly killed more than 50 people. Paris described the attacks as evidence of Russia's escalation and pledged to support efforts to hold those responsible accountable.

items.title: Border guards destroy Murom surveillance system, Russian drone launch site in Sumy region
items.teaser: Fighters from the Steel Border border brigade in Ukraine's Sumy region destroyed a Murom surveillance system and a launch site for Russian drones.

items.teaser: ASTRA also reported damage to a residential building in Rostov-on-Don's Donskaya Sloboda complex, identifying its location through footage posted by residents. It remained unclear what struck the building amid reports of continued drone activity and Russian air defense operations.

items.title: Red Cross to fund evacuation of around 90 rural households from Donetsk region
items.teaser: Around 90 rural households in Ukrainian-controlled areas of the Donetsk region will receive financial assistance from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to evacuate livestock, poultry and equipment.

items.title: US, Ukrainian, European officials discuss ending Russia's war at Miami meeting
items.teaser: The meeting coincided with U.S. President Donald Trump's announcement that Russia would supply millions of tons of diesel to the United States and global markets following a call with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

items.title: Russian forces forcibly remove 25 residents from occupied part of Kharkiv region – Lubinets
items.teaser: Russian troops have taken 25 residents, including children, from the temporarily occupied part of the Kharkiv region under the pretext of a so-called "evacuation." Their whereabouts are currently unknown.

items.title: Why won’t the world call Russia’s theft of Ukrainian children genocide? A Ukrainian lawyer has the evidence, and says only the will is missing.
items.teaser: Kateryna Rashevska can walk you through exactly how one Ukrainian child disappears into Russia: the occupied-territory orphanage, the foster placement with a Kremlin-connected family, the re-education camp, the military uniform, the draft notice that arrives at sixteen.

items.title: Koretskyi, German ambassador discuss supply of equipment for restoring Ukraine’s energy system
items.teaser: Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi met with Germany’s ambassador to Ukraine, Boris Ruge.

items.title: Russia increasing number and geographic reach of attacks using jet-powered drones – Ukrainian Air Force
items.teaser: Russian occupation forces have recently been increasing the proportion of jet-powered drones used in attacks across Ukraine. The geographic scope of their use is also expanding.

items.title: Trump kündigt russische Diesel-Lieferungen an
items.teaser: Wegen der hohen Spritpreise steht Trump innenpolitisch unter wachsendem Druck. Nun verkündet der US-Präsident einen Deal mit Russland, der die Lieferung von zunächst 300.000 Tonnen Diesel für die USA und den Weltmarkt umfasst. Kiew ist empört.

items.title: Ukrainians in Rome hold charity dinner to raise funds for AFU
items.teaser: During the sixth charity “Warm Dinner” event in Rome, Ukrainians raised 2,880 euros to purchase medications, medical supplies, and equipment for a stabilization center run by a unit of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.

items.title: "It looks like a happy birthday present for Putin": Zelenskyy criticises US approval of Russian diesel imports
items.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Washington's move to ease restrictions on Russian diesel exports will provide Moscow with more money to finance its war. The decision follows a phone call between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin and has caused concern among Ukraine's government and European leaders.

items.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1689: Russia plans up to 1,000 missiles, drones, and bombs against 60 Ukrainian infrastructure sites this winter, Ukraine says
items.teaser: Ukrainian forces rerun the Vivaldi playbook outside Kramatorsk and push Russia back across the Siverskyi Donets, drones hit a Kh-101 fuel plant and a far-north refinery inside Russia, and Russian strikes on warehouses, a store, and a farm kill three.

items.title: Zelensky: Ukrainian negotiating team used as “smokescreen” amid US-Russia diesel deal
items.teaser: Commenting on U.S. President Donald Trump’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel, President Volodymyr Zelensky said the Ukrainian negotiating team currently in Florida holding peace talks is being used as a “smokescreen,” and “that is definitely not fair.”

items.title: Zelensky appoints former European integration minister Kachka as EU ambassador
items.teaser: During Kachka’s tenure overseeing EU integration, Ukraine opened its first two accession negotiation clusters — groups of policy areas in which candidates must meet EU requirements.

items.title: Zelensky: Letting Russia sell fuel means investing in its war
items.teaser: Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world; Russia will “repay” the diesel gesture with further terror and atrocities.

items.title: Zelenskyy: Ukrainian negotiating team used as "cover" amid Trump-Putin deal
items.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticises Washington's decision to allow Russian diesel exports while Ukrainian officials are negotiating in the US. He says the revenue from fuel sales will help Moscow finance its war against Ukraine.

items.title: US agrees on diesel fuel supplies from Russia
items.teaser: Russia will immediately supply 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the global market with US approval and substantially increase its exports in the future.

items.title: Putin plans further cooperation after diesel deal with Trump
items.teaser: Following a phone call with Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin has confirmed Russia's readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to US and global markets. The Kremlin also says the two leaders agreed to maintain contact and discussed the war in Ukraine and the situation around Iran.

items.title: Kyiv boosts public security and increases patrols
items.teaser: Kyiv is stepping up public security measures and increasing the number of National Police and National Guard patrols on city streets after dark.

items.title: Investigators say prosecutors shielded scam call centers. Their office has now fired eight people and is checking how its ex-chief left Ukraine
items.teaser: The acting chief also ordered out a deputy at the regional office he ran until September and dropped no-contest hiring of outsiders.

items.title: Zelenskyy: Russia will "repay" diesel concessions with further terror and perfidy

items.title: Kyiv protests Belarus’s summoning of Ukraine’s chargé d’affaires
items.teaser: Kyiv has lodged a protest over Belarus’s summoning of Ukraine’s chargé d’affaires in the Republic of Belarus to the Belarusian Foreign Ministry.

items.title: Trump says Russia agreed to supply millions of tons of diesel to US and global markets as he blames Ukraine for fuel price hikes driven by the Iran war
items.teaser: The announcement comes as Trump pressures Kyiv to halt attacks on Russian oil infrastructure, which Ukraine targets to weaken Moscow’s war economy.

items.title: Trump, Putin agree on deal to release Russian diesel to US, world markets
items.teaser: Russia will supply diesel to global markets in a bid to lower prices, US President Donald Trump has said. The move reverses years of pressure on the Russian economy following the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

items.title: German Bundestag recognizes Germany’s special historical responsibility to Ukraine for Nazi crimes
items.teaser: The German Bundestag has recognized Germany’s special historical responsibility to Ukraine for the crimes of National Socialism, adopting two motions ahead of the 85th anniversary of the Babyn Yar massacre: one submitted by the governing CDU/CSU and SPD parties, and the other by the opposition Greens.

items.title: Head of Russian military propaganda network to be expelled from Montenegro over suspected anti-EU operation
items.teaser: Authorities ordered Mikhail Zvynchuk, founder of the Russian military-focused Rybar network, and four associates to leave the country after seizing drones and recording equipment.

items.title: Zelensky discusses Graham Act, anti-ballistic missile production with U.S. congressional delegation

items.title: Trump says Russia agreed to supply millions of tons of diesel to US, global markets

items.teaser: A man was killed in an airstrike by Russian forces in Ivano-Frankivsk, and a fire broke out after debris from a drone fell.

items.title: Russia loses 1,710 soldiers over past day
items.teaser: Ukraine's General Staff has updated data on Russian losses: Russia lost 1,710 soldiers killed and wounded over the past day.

items.title: Ukraine reportedly targets Russian cruise missile fuel plant in Tver Oblast
items.teaser: Ukraine's military launched an attack on Russia's Tver Oblast overnight on Oct. 9, reportedly targeting a Russian factory that manufactures fuel components for Kh-55 and Kh-101 cruise missiles, Russian Telegram media channels reported.

items.title: Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, October 8, 2026
items.teaser: Toplines Russian milbloggers recently acknowledged Ukrainian advances east of Slovyansk and Kramatorsk, possibly after months of battlefield shaping efforts similar to those which Ukrainian forces conducted…

items.title: MoD: Thousands of service members return from AWOL under simplified procedure
items.teaser: Thousands of service members have returned to their units under a simplified reintegration program following absence without leave (AWOL).

items.title: Was die ukrainischen Angriffe auf Russland bewirken
items.teaser: Immer wieder trifft die Ukraine russische Energieanlagen. Sicherheitsexperte Nico Lange erklärt die Strategie dahinter - und wie die Angriffe die russische Abwehr überwinden.

items.title: Aktuelles zum Krieg in der Ukraine
items.teaser: Seit Februar 2022 führt Russland einen Angriffskrieg gegen die Ukraine, die Kämpfe dauern an. Alle Entwicklungen und Ukraine-News im Liveticker.

items.title: Ukraine, Europe, US to meet in Miami for talks on ending war
items.teaser: Officials from Ukraine, Europe and the US are meeting in Miami to discuss ways to break the deadlock in the war. The meeting comes as Russian strikes on Ukraine killed more than 70 people this week.

items.title: One killed and five injured in Russian guided bomb strike on Zaporizhzhia – photos, video
items.teaser: One person has been killed and five injured in a Russian guided aerial bomb attack on the city of Zaporizhzhia on the morning of 9 October.

items.title: Politico: Over 100,000 Ukrainians in US face threat of deportation
items.teaser: US President Donald Trump's administration must decide by 19 October whether to extend or cancel Temporary Protected Status for over 100,000 Ukrainians who fled the war.

items.title: UK to provide $71 million winter aid package to Ukraine
items.teaser: The latest announcement comes as Kyiv experienced widespread power outages on Oct. 8 following a Russian attack on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Over 3 million residents in the capital lost power in what officials described as "an attack on one of the energy facilities important for the city of Kyiv."

items.title: Ukraine returns 2,665 children taken by Russia
items.teaser: Since the start of Russia’s full-scale war, 20,651 cases of the deportation and/or forced transfer of children have been recorded, while efforts undertaken so far have enabled 2,665 children to be returned to Ukraine.

items.title: US-Luftwaffe betreibt Stützpunkt: Festnahmen nach Zaundurchbruch an Militärbasis in Großbritannien
items.teaser: Der britische Stützpunkt Molesworth wird vom US-Militär genutzt. Dort befinden sich auch Nato-Geheimdiensteinrichtungen. Zwei Männer dringen unbefugt in den Sicherheitsbereich ein. Sie wollten "dem Vereinigten Königreich Schaden zufügen", erklärt die Anti-Terror-Polizei.

items.title: Verhandlungsteam der Ukraine reist zu Gesprächen in die USA
items.teaser: Eine ukrainische Delegation will in den USA mit Trumps Unterhändlern über einen Vorschlag für ein Ende des Ukraine-Krieges beraten. Auch europäische Vertreter sollen teilnehmen.

items.title: Pollsters name two leaders in electoral support
items.teaser: Volodymyr Zelensky and Valerii Zaluzhnyi lead in electoral support, with 22.9% and 20.2%, respectively.

items.title: UK service member charged with spying for Russia makes first court appearance
items.teaser: Under the U.K.'s National Security Act 2023, junior intelligence specialist Teddy Young, 24, was charged with two offenses for allegedly trying to pass protected information to a foreign power between November 2024 and May 2025.

items.title: Half a tonne each: Police neutralize two unexploded ballistic missiles that fell near homes in Kyiv
items.teaser: Explosives experts from the Kyiv police have neutralized two unexploded ballistic missiles used by Russian forces to attack the city on October 7.

items.title: Ex-German Chancellor Schröder attends Putin's birthday bash
items.teaser: Former Chancellor Gerhard Schröder still maintains a friendship with Russian leader Vladimir Putin. Tensions are high between Germany and Russia as the invasion of Ukraine continues.

items.title: Ukraine's Foreign Ministry seeks answers over detention of UP journalist Mykhailo Tkach in Vienna
items.teaser: Embassy of Ukraine in Austria has asked Austrian authorities to explain the detention of Ukrainska Pravda investigative journalist Mykhailo Tkach. He remains in custody despite a Ukrainian consul having met with him.

items.title: Serviceman recruited by Russia while AWOL detained for directing strikes on Ukrainian forces
items.teaser: Investigators with the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) have served a Ukrainian Armed Forces serviceman with a notice of suspicion for passing information about the locations of Ukrainian military units to Russian intelligence services.

items.title: Armored assaults aren’t dead. Robots got the credit, but it was Ukrainian infantry in armored trucks that reversed a year of Russian gains near Lyman
items.teaser: Robots cleared the mines and blew up the bunkers, but soldiers still had to ride in and hold the ground.

items.title: Ukraine to participate in Future Forces international arms exhibition and forum in Prague
items.teaser: Ukraine will be one of the largest participants in the 16th International “Future Forces” Exhibition & Forum (Future Forces Exhibition & Forum 2026), which will take place in Prague on October 21–23.

items.title: Guard killed in Russian Shahed drone attack on Ivano-Frankivsk
items.teaser: A man working as a security guard was killed when debris from a downed Russian drone fell on an office building in Ivano-Frankivsk on the evening of 8 October.

items.title: Two trains collide in Lviv, injuring 8
items.teaser: The railway operator initially reported that the passenger train's driver suffered a leg injury and four passengers required medical attention. The crew of the electric locomotive was unharmed.

items.title: Russia will pay the price for strikes on Pryluky and Kramatorsk – Zelensky
items.teaser: Ukraine will not strike Russian children, as Russian dictator Putin's criminal regime does, but "certain adults" will soon receive a response.

items.title: Ukrainian investigative journalist Mykhailo Tkach detained in Austria while on assignment
items.teaser: The acclaimed journalist was reportedly on an editorial assignment in Vienna with his colleague Yaroslav Bondarenko when he was detained by Austrian authorities.

items.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1688: Russian strike on two passenger buses kills 30 in Kramatorsk
items.teaser: The Pryluky death toll reached 22, including five children, as rescuers finished searching the rubble, while blackouts returned to Kyiv and ISW warned that faster jet-powered Gerans are freeing Russia to concentrate missiles for its winter campaign against Ukraine’s energy.

items.title: Khmara, Pistorius discuss Ukraine's key needs to protect critical infrastructure
items.teaser: Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara and German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius discussed Ukraine's key needs to protect critical infrastructure, particularly in Kyiv, during a phone call.

items.title: Russischer Investigativjournalist erhält Leipziger Medienpreis
items.teaser: Der russische Journalist Roman Dobrokhotov ist in Leipzig mit dem "Preis für die Freiheit und Zukunft der Medien" ausgezeichnet worden. Er gilt in seiner Heimat als "ausländischer Agent".

items.title: UK to provide GBP 54M in winter support to Ukraine
items.teaser: UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, during his first visit to Kyiv in his current role, reaffirmed Britain's unwavering support for Ukraine and announced GBP 54 million ($71.3 million) in funding to strengthen the country's resilience ahead of winter.

items.title: UP investigative journalist Mykhailo Tkach detained in Vienna while on editorial assignment
items.teaser: Ukrainska Pravda investigative journalist Mykhailo Tkach has been detained in Vienna while on an editorial assignment. The outlet demands his immediate release.

items.title: Diesel train collides with electric locomotive in Lviv, casualties reported
items.teaser: A Lviv-Sokal diesel train collided with an electric locomotive while departing from Pidzamche station in Lviv, injuring several people.

items.title: Moldova pulls its border officers off Ukrainian soil again as Russian drones keep hitting crossings
items.teaser: “They will work on the territory of Moldova.” Moldovan Interior Minister Daniela Misail-Nikitin, on withdrawing border personnel from Ukraine.

items.title: Zelensky: Strike on Yandex data center was a mirror response to Russia's actions
items.teaser: Ukraine carried out a mirror strike on a Yandex data center in response to similar actions by the Russian Federation.

items.title: Kremlin agrees with Rubio on lack of prospects for diplomatic settlement
items.teaser: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov says Moscow agrees with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio that there are currently no prospects for a diplomatic settlement, while accusing Ukraine of being unwilling to pursue peace.

items.title: Ukrainian negotiating team to meet Witkoff, Kushner in US on Oct 9
items.teaser: The Ukrainian negotiating team will meet with Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff in the United States on Friday, October 9.

items.title: 'We always respond in kind' — Zelensky addresses Ukrainian attacks on Russian data center
items.teaser: "We certainly are capable," Zelensky said about striking Russian data centers. "We always respond in kind. Regarding data centers, as you all know, they have been and still are striking our data centers."

items.title: Two killed in Russian drone strike on car in Kramatorsk
items.teaser: Russian forces struck a car with a drone in central Kramatorsk, Donetsk region, on Thursday evening, October 8, killing two people.

items.title: Over 130 children remain in mandatory evacuation zone in de-occupied part of Kherson region
items.teaser: A total of 132 children remain in the mandatory evacuation zone in the de-occupied part of the Kherson region. Some of them have not yet been evacuated due to the difficult security situation.

items.title: Zelensky sends delegation to meet Trump envoys as he hints at secret US-Russia economic talks
items.teaser: "Meetings are expected to take place over two days... we are counting on a European team to join our negotiating group," President Volodymyr Zelensky said.

items.title: Blackouts return to Kyiv as Russia prepares to freeze civilians over the winter
items.teaser: Russia is once again targeting Ukraine’s energy infrastructure as winter approaches, threatening to leave civilians without power, heat, and water as Moscow ramps up its campaign to cripple the country’s critical systems.

items.title: Russia lifts quarantine in Irkutsk region, where lab worker allegedly died of plague
items.teaser: Initial reports raised concerns that 28-year-old Darya Shipilova, who worked at the Anti-Plague Institute, might have died of pneumonic plague after a laboratory accident.

items.title: Zelenskyy: European partners to join Ukrainian negotiating team in US
items.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has stated on 8 October that European partners will join the Ukrainian negotiating team during talks in the United States on 9-10 October.

items.title: Selenskyj: ukrainische Unterhändler reisen am Freitag in die USA
items.teaser: Das ukrainische Verhandlungsteam arbeitet heute in Europa und morgen oder übermorgen, am 9.–10. Oktober, wird es in den USA sein, sagte der Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj während eines Besuchs im nordukrainischen Pryluky nach einem tödlichen russischen Angriff auf die Stadt.

items.teaser: Some of those killed in a Russian strike on two buses in Kramatorsk have yet to be identified due to the severity of their injuries.

items.teaser: The Trump administration recently announced that it has invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to December's G20 summit in Miami. items.title: UK allocates £54 million for Ukraine's winter resilience
items.teaser: UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has announced a £54 million funding package during his first visit to Ukraine on 8 October to bolster the country's energy and humanitarian resilience over the winter.

items.title: "The issue is survival": Mayor Klitschko advises Kyiv residents to consider leaving capital
items.teaser: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko has stated on 8 October that Kyiv is facing a matter of survival amid intensifying Russian attacks and advised residents who can to temporarily relocate outside the capital.

items.title: Parliament, Government set key bills needed for Ukraine’s funding
items.teaser: The Verkhovna Rada and the Cabinet of Ministers have agreed on legislative priorities ahead of the parliamentary plenary week, including bills needed to fulfill Ukraine’s international commitments and secure financial support from partners.

items.title: Ukraine war latest: Russian glide bomb strikes in Kramatorsk kill at least 33
items.teaser: Key developments on Oct. 8: At least 33 dead after Russian glide bomb strikes Kramatorsk buses Russian drone barrage on Kyiv kills 4, injures 19, disrupts electricity, water supplies Polish SIM cards found in Russian drones downed in Poland US, Russia confirm Trump's latest Ukraine peace push is

items.title: Lithuania puts up to 100 soldiers on Kaliningrad border as officials brace for possible Russian mobilization
items.teaser: The move comes as Moscow rejects reports of a new call-up while Ukrainian officials warn Russia is preparing to expand its forces.

items.title: Ukrainian medics learn about the Dutch model of care for premature babies
items.teaser: Ukrainian medical professionals visited Emma Children’s Hospital (Emma Kinderziekenhuis) in Amsterdam, which is part of Amsterdam UMC, one of the largest university medical centers in the Netherlands. items.title: Ukrainian pilots to begin training on Rafale fighter jets in France in November
items.teaser: French Armed Forces Minister Catherine Vautrin has announced on 8 October that Ukrainian pilots will begin training on French Rafale fighter jets in France in November.

items.title: Russians kill two more people in Kramatorsk, bringing city's daily death toll to 32
items.teaser: Two more people have been killed in a Russian drone strike on a civilian car in Kramatorsk, Donetsk Oblast, on the evening of 8 October, bringing the city's total death toll for the day to 32.

items.title: Russian attacks plunge Kyiv into near-total darkness, disrupt power, metro, water supply
items.teaser: The drop in voltage temporarily halted Kyiv Metro train services and escalator operations, the Kyiv City State Administration (KMDA) said. Other parts of the capital's public transport network were also affected.

items.title: Four killed, 19 injured in Kyiv in Russian attacks throughout day
items.teaser: Four people were killed and 19 others injured in Russian attacks on the capital throughout Thursday, October 8.

items.title: Live: Was die Angriffe der Ukraine bewirken
items.teaser: Die Ukraine trifft nach eigenen Angaben Russlands größte Öl-Raffinerie und auch ein Rechenzentrum des Tech-Unternehmens Yandex. ZDFheute live dazu, was die Angriffe bewirken.

items.title: Ukraine greift 2400 Kilometer entfernte Ölraffinerie in Russland an
items.teaser: Die ukrainischen Verteidigungskräfte haben am 8. Oktober die größte Ölanlage Russlands – die Ölraffinerie in Omsk angegriffen, teilt der Generalstab auf Facebook mit.

items.title: Russia attacks one of Kyiv’s key energy facilities – Energy Minister
items.teaser: Russian forces attacked one of the energy facilities that is important for Kyiv.

items.title: Anti-drone electronic warfare systems by Ukraine's Phantom Defense tested in Pentagon programme
items.teaser: Electronic warfare systems developed by Ukrainian defence tech company Phantom Defense have been tested in the US during the second stage of the Pentagon's Drone Dominance programme.

items.title: Ukraine preparing response to new wave of Russian escalation – Zelensky
items.teaser: Ukraine is preparing a response to a new wave of Russian escalation and is working with partners to secure additional air defense packages and ammunition for F-16 fighter jets.

items.title: Spionage-Verdacht - Kontrollgremium des Bundestags fordert Konsequenzen aus dem Fall Hanning
items.teaser: Das Parlamentarische Kontrollgremium des Bundestags hat die Bundesregierung aufgefordert, aus dem Spionageverdacht gegen den früheren BND-Präsidenten Hanning Konsequenzen zu ziehen.

items.title: Sybiha shares details of talks with UK foreign secretary at Pryluky hospital
items.teaser: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has shared details of his talks with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, which took place at a hospital in Pryluky, Chernihiv Oblast, on 8 October.

items.title: Drei Tote und zwei Verletzte nach russischem Angriff auf Baumarkt in Kyjiw
items.teaser: Im Stadtteil Solomjanskyj in Kyjiw sind bei einem russischen Angriff auf einen Baumarkt drei Menschen getötet worden. Zwei weitere Menschen wurden verletzt, teilte die Polizeibehörde auf Facebook mit.

items.title: Zelensky, Costa discuss Russian strikes, EU aid, opening of negotiating clusters
items.teaser: President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky and European Council President António Costa discussed the schedule for opening the next negotiating clusters on Ukraine’s accession to the EU, as well as an energy package for the winter and further financial support.

items.title: Two 14-year-old boys killed by an explosive device in a field in Sumy Oblast
items.teaser: Residents are being warned that, in addition to constant Russian attacks, there is a risk of encountering explosive devices.

items.title: Verteidigungskräfte melden Treffer auf Signalverstärker des russischen Mesh-Netzwerks im Schwarzen Meer
items.teaser: Die ukrainischen Verteidigungskräfte haben am 7. Oktober und in der Nacht zum 8. Oktober eine Reihe wichtiger militärischer Objekte Russlands, insbesondere einen Signalverstärker des russischen Mesh-Netzwerks im Schwarzen Meer getroffen.

items.title: Ukraine open to restoring dialogue with South Korea despite Seoul’s decision to recall ambassador – MFA
items.teaser: Ukraine remains open to restoring constructive dialogue with the Republic of Korea despite Seoul’s decision to recall its ambassador to Ukraine, Park Kichang, over the situation involving North Korean prisoners of war.

items.title: Zelenskyy: We are preparing our responses to this wave of Russian escalation
items.teaser: Following reports from the Security Service and the President's Office on 8 October, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine is preparing responses to the current wave of Russian escalation.

items.title: Major internet outage hits Russia after strike on Yandex data center
items.teaser: A major outage has disrupted Russia’s internet segment.

items.title: Russian attack on Zaporizhzhia kills car driver and injures three adults and two children
items.teaser: A car driver has been killed and five people, including two children, have been injured in Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia on the evening of 8 October.

items.title: Some public transport services halted in Kyiv following metro suspension
items.teaser: Some public transport services in Kyiv have been temporarily suspended on 8 October due to a drop in voltage in the power grid, following earlier disruptions on the Kyiv Metro.

items.title: Ukrainian Foreign Ministry on recall of South Korean ambassador: Ukraine is open to resuming dialogue
items.teaser: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has stated that Kyiv remains open to resuming constructive dialogue despite Seoul's decision to recall its ambassador to Ukraine.

items.title: Oleshky situation shows limits of dialogue between Ukrainian and Russian Ombudsmen
items.teaser: The situation in Oleshky has demonstrated the limits of what dialogue between the institutions of the Ukrainian and Russian ombudsmen can achieve in the context of carrying out a large-scale humanitarian operation.

items.title: 80% of Moldovans say country is unprepared for attack as Russian drones flow into its airspace, but few back NATO membership
items.teaser: A new poll shows widespread concern over Moldova’s ability to withstand an attack, even as only 4% of respondents see NATO membership as the answer. Russian drones have increasingly crossed Moldovan airspace in recent weeks.

items.title: Moldova ready to take in more Ukrainian refugees come winter, Sandu says
items.teaser: "If this winter in Ukraine is as difficult as the whole world expects, we are ready to receive as many people as need safety," Moldovan President Maia Sandu said at the Moldova Security Forum in Chisinau on Oct. 8.

items.title: Südkorea zieht Botschafter aus Kyjiw ab
items.teaser: Wegen eines diplomatischen Streits mit der Ukraine hat Südkorea seinen Botschafter aus Kyjiw abgezogen, heisst es in einer Erklärung des südkoreanischen Außenministeriums, wie die Nachrichtenagentur Yonhap berichtet.

items.title: Kyiv Metro halts train services due to voltage drop
items.teaser: Train services and escalators on the Kyiv Metro have been temporarily suspended on 8 October due to a drop in voltage from external power sources.
